venue: Citi Field (Flushing/Queens, New York, NY). CONFIRMED as the current and only home ballpark of the New York Mets as of the 2026 season. Name is current: RateYourSeats, MLB.com and Ballparks of Baseball all use 'Citi Field' in 2026-dated content, and the RateYourSeats venue page lists a full 2026 Mets home schedule at Citi Field (e.g. 'Washington Nationals at New York Mets, Citi Field - Flushing, NY, Aug 16 2026'). Ballparks of Baseball lists '-Former Name(s): None' and naming rights held by Citigroup at $20 million/year for 20 years from 2009. No rename or relocation found.
concert_only_sections: Field Seats (concert floor). RateYourSeats' Citi Field section index contains a group 'All Field Seats Sections' whose single entry, 'Field Sections', links to https://www.rateyourseats.com/citi-field/seating/field-seats and is labelled elsewhere on the site as 'Concert Field Seats for Concerts'. The individual floor-section labels (e.g. F1, A1) are NOT enumerated anywhere on the RateYourSeats venue section index, so no concert floor section IDs can be recorded. Source: https://www.rateyourseats.com/citi-field/seating/sections
capacity: Conflicting figures. (1) Wikipedia, article body: 'Citi Field has a capacity of 41,922.' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citi_Field). (2) Wikipedia infobox also lists '41,800 (2009-2011)' as the original capacity and '45,000+ (including standing room)'. (3) Ballparks of Baseball, Facts & Figures: '-Capacity: 42,000' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/citi-field/). (4) Record attendance figures cited by Wikipedia: 44,859 (postseason), 44,466 (regular season, 2016), 43,700 (Aug 3 2023 concert). RECOMMENDED: 41,922 (current listed seating capacity; 42,000 is a rounded restatement of the same figure and 41,800 is the superseded 2009-2011 figure).

orientation.batter_faces: North-northeast. The batter at home plate looks out toward center field to the north-northeast; the sun rises over right field, tracks down the first-base line during the morning, passes over home plate at midday and sets behind the third-base stands, making the third-base line the shade side and the first-base line and right field the sunny side.
orientation.confidence: medium-high (single explicit source, but consistent with the official Mets gate geography: the Right Field Gate is on the 1st base side and the Left Field Gate on the 3rd base side, and with the 7 Train / Jackie Robinson Rotunda sitting behind home plate)
orientation.source: https://www.shadedseats.com/citi-field-shaded-seats/ - 'Citi Field is oriented to the north-northeast. The sun rises over right field and progresses down the 1st baseline during the morning. It curves around home plate at mid-day and ultimately sets behind the 3rd base stands.'

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE FROM THE RIGHT-FIELD / FIRST-BASE SIDE TOWARD THE THIRD-BASE / LEFT-FIELD SIDE, i.e. they increase TOWARD THIRD BASE. LOW numbers = right field and the first-base side. HIGH numbers = third base, left field, then center field. Every numbering series at Citi Field runs the SAME direction; none is reversed. Ballpark E-Guides states it in one sentence: 'The numbering starts with 101 and 301 in right field and increases clockwise around the ballpark. The Promenade level starts in the right field corner with 401 and 501. The numbering continues until the Big Apple Reserved seats in center field at 140-142.' Per-series detail: (a) FIELD LEVEL 100s: 101 in right field -> 107 at the right-field foul-line end of the protective fence -> 111-114 first base side behind the Mets dugout -> 115-117 first base side, 117 closest to home plate -> HOME PLATE between 117 and 118 -> 118-120 third base side, 118 closest to home plate -> 121-124 third base side behind the visiting dugout -> 127/128 at the left-field foul-line end of the fence -> 129-132 down the left-field line -> 133-139 left field -> 140-142 Big Apple Reserved in center field -> 143 Citi Pavilion in right-center field near Shea Bridge (the series wraps the outfield and terminates just short of where it began). (b) SINGLE/DOUBLE-DIGIT PREMIUM SERIES 11-19 (Clover Home Plate Club, Sterling Level): sits directly behind home plate between the Delta Sky360 field-level seats and the Field Level; runs the same way, low toward first base and high toward third base, consistent with the surrounding levels; RateYourSeats section 19 carries a fan review reading 'Best seats for fans of the visiting team. Right next to the on deck circle' which places 19 on the visiting/third-base end of the 11-19 run. (c) EXCELSIOR LEVEL 300s: 301-305 (Coca-Cola Corner) in right field -> 309-312 first base side -> 315 first base side -> HOME PLATE around 319-320 -> 324 third base side -> 326-329 third base side -> 329 in the left-field corner -> 334-339 (The Porch / former Left Field Landing) in left field. (d) PROMENADE 400s: 401 in the right-field corner -> 411 first base side -> 415 behind home plate -> 418 third base side -> 429 in the left-field corner -> 437 high end. (e) PROMENADE 500s: 501-505 outfield on the right-field side -> 511 first base side -> 514 behind home plate -> 518 third base side -> 532-538 outfield on the left-field side. All five series therefore AGREE: low = right field / first base, high = left field / third base.

anchors.where: RIGHT FIELD. Ballpark E-Guides: 'The numbering starts with 101 and 301 in right field and increases clockwise around the ballpark.' RateYourSeats section 101 is an outfield/Outfield Reserved section (photo captions 'bullpen view from 101', 'shaded outfield seats', file prefix citifield-outfieldreserved) and is tagged 'Top Pick for Visiting Team Fans'. Shaded Seats independently places 101-103 in right field: 'Rows deep in sections 101-103 in right field also benefit from the overhang of the mezzanine section above.'

RIGHT FIELD, Excelsior (mezzanine) level, beyond the right-field wall. RateYourSeats: 'Right Field Upper Deck: Located in Sections 301-305 beyond the right-field wall' and 'The Coca-Cola Corner is located in Sections 301-305 in right field at Citi Field, positioned beyond the outfield wall on the upper deck.' Ballpark E-Guides agrees: 'The Coca-Cola Corner in right field is Sections 301-305' and 'the Coca-Cola Corner is that five sections of seats in the Excelsior level in right field, which hang over the Right Field Reserved seats.' Cross-checked against the official Mets accessibility guide, which places Guest Elevators D and E at 'Excelsior Level at Section 306 / Ramp to Coca-Cola Corner' on the same elevator run that serves 'Field Level at Section 109' and 'Promenade Level at Sections 403 & 503' - all low-numbered, all first-base/right-field side.

FIRST BASE SIDE - official Mets statement. Citi Field Accessibility Guide, 'Elevator Information for Elevators B and C': 'Delta Level at the Delta Sky360 Club - First Base side / Field Level at Section 114 / Hyundai Club First Base entrance / Excelsior Level at Section 315 / Heineken Diamond Lounge First Base entrance / Promenade Level at Section 411 & 511.' This single official listing fixes the first-base side simultaneously for the 100, 300, 400 and 500 series.

BEHIND HOME PLATE, Field Level - home plate falls between 117 and 118. RateYourSeats Hyundai Club: 'First Base Side: Sections 115, 116, and 117 run down the first base line, with Section 117 positioned closest to home plate. These sections sit nearest to the Mets dugout.' and 'Third Base Side: Sections 118, 119, and 120 extend down the third base line, with Section 118 located closest to home plate. These seats are positioned on the visitor dugout side of the field.' and 'Sections 117 and 118 sit closest to home plate and offer the most centered views within the Hyundai Club.' Independently corroborated by a RateYourSeats fan-feedback note repeated on many Citi Field section pages: 'The netting extends from sections 111-124' - a range whose midpoint is 117/118.

BEHIND HOME PLATE, Excelsior (300) level. RateYourSeats section 320 Section Insights list 'Home Plate View' and the Seating Notes read 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'. Bracketed by the official Mets elevator listings: Excelsior 315 = First Base side (Elevators B/C), Excelsior 324 = Third Base side (Elevators P/Q).

BEHIND HOME PLATE, Promenade 400 level. RateYourSeats section 415 Section Insights list 'Home Plate View'; Seating Notes: 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'. RateYourSeats Promenade Level: 'Promenade Silver: Sections 411-418 (behind home plate)'. Bracketed by official Mets elevator listings: Promenade 411 = First Base side, Promenade 418 = Third Base side.

BEHIND HOME PLATE, Promenade 500 level. RateYourSeats section 514 Section Insights list 'Home Plate View'; Seating Notes: 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'. RateYourSeats Promenade Level: 'Promenade Infield: Sections 510-518 ... which provide the most centered perspective of the field.' Bracketed by official Mets elevator listings: Promenade 511 = First Base side, Promenade 518 = Third Base side.

THIRD BASE SIDE - official Mets statement. Citi Field Accessibility Guide, 'Guest Elevators P and Q': 'Plaza Level at the Seaver Entrance / Delta Level at the Delta Sky360 Club - Third Base side / Field Level at Section 121 / Hyundai Club Third Base entrance / Empire Level at Suite 227 / Excelsior Level at Section 324 / Heineken Diamond Lounge Third Base entrance / Promenade Level at Sections 418 & 518.' Mirrors the Elevators B/C first-base listing and fixes the third-base side for the 100, 300, 400 and 500 series at once.

LEFT FIELD CORNER - official Mets statement. Citi Field Accessibility Guide, Ramps: 'The Left Field Ramp is available for all guests and provides access to all levels of Citi Field. It is located in the left field corner behind sections 129, 329, and 429.' One sentence anchoring the left-field corner on three different levels.

anchors.section: 334-339 (The Porch, formerly Left Field Landing / Thomas Tew / Budweiser Landing)
anchors.where: LEFT FIELD, Excelsior level, beyond the left-field wall. RateYourSeats: 'Left Field Upper Deck Seating: Located in Sections 334-339 beyond the left-field wall' and 'The Porch is made up of Sections 334-339 in left field at Citi Field. This area has been known by several names over the years, including Thomas Tew, Budweiser Landing, and Left Field Landing.' Officially corroborated: the Mets accessibility guide lists 'Guest Elevator K ... Excelsior Level at Section 334 (this is the only elevator that provides access to Thomas Tew Reserve- Sections 334-339)', and Ballpark E-Guides independently says 'Left Field Landing seats are on the Excelsior level in left field.'

CENTER FIELD and RIGHT-CENTER FIELD - the high end of the 100 series wraps past left field through center back toward right-center. Ballpark E-Guides: 'The numbering continues until the Big Apple Reserved seats in center field at 140-142.' RateYourSeats Big Apple Reserved: 'Center Field Location: Situated just to the right of the Home Run Apple beyond the outfield wall.' RateYourSeats Citi Pavilion (section 143): 'Right-Center Field Location: Situated just beyond the outfield wall near Shea Bridge' and 'Bullpen Views: Positioned directly behind the Mets bullpens.' Officially corroborated: the Mets accessibility guide places 'Elevator J ... Plaza Level at Bullpen Plaza / Field Level at Section 142' and a Fan Assistance Station at 'Section 142 next to the Shea Bridge'.

DUGOUT-LEVEL CONFIRMATION of direction. RateYourSeats Metropolitan Club: 'Sections 111-114 sit on the first base side directly behind the Mets dugout.' / 'Sections 121-124 are positioned on the third base side directly behind the visiting team dugout.' Low numbers first base, high numbers third base.
EXCELSIOR-LEVEL CONFIRMATION of direction. RateYourSeats Excelsior Box: 'First Base Side: Sections 309-312' / 'Third Base Side: Sections 326-329'.

numbering_direction.confidence: very high. Three fully independent source families agree and none dissents: (1) the official Mets Citi Field Accessibility Guide on mlb.com, whose elevator, ramp and gate listings name first-base-side and third-base-side sections explicitly on all four numbered levels; (2) RateYourSeats zone pages (Metropolitan Club, Hyundai Club, Excelsior Box, Coca-Cola Corner, The Porch, Citi Pavilion, Big Apple Reserved); (3) Ballpark E-Guides, which states the rule outright. No source anywhere places 101 or 301 in left field or 143 in left field.

Empire Suite Level (Sterling Suites 1-10: TIER DOES NOT PROVIDE GENERAL TICKETED SEATING - suites only; no home-plate anchor should be configured. The RateYourSeats section index lists Sterling Suites 1-10 under 'All Empire Suites Sections' and they all link to the zone page rather than to individual section pages, so no per-section geometry is available.

levels.name: Delta Sky360 Club (field level, behind home plate)
levels.sections: A, AA, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, HH (RateYourSeats slugs club_a, club_aa, club_b, club_c, club_d, club_e, club_f, club_g, club_h, club_hh; the index labels them 'Home Plate Club A' ... 'Home Plate Club HH')
levels.notes: 'The Delta Sky360 Club features the closest seats to the field at Citi Field, located directly behind home plate in the first eight rows of Sections A-H as well as sections AA and HH.' Ordering along the arc, verbatim: 'Sections AA & A are closest to the Mets dugout', 'Sections C & E are centered directly behind the plate', 'Sections H & HH are closest to the visitor dugout'. Since the Mets dugout is on the first base side, AA/A are the first-base end and H/HH the third-base end - same low-to-high direction as the numeric series. Ballpark E-Guides describes this as 'nine sections of those padded, comfortable monsters directly behind home plate' and notes 'the last rows of Delta sections have seats in front of aisles, making for an awful obstructed views with people walking in front of you. Avoid Row 20.'

levels.name: Clover Home Plate Club (Sterling Level) - sections 11-19
levels.notes: 'The Clover Home Plate Club is located in Sections 11-19 directly behind home plate at Citi Field, positioned just behind the field-level Delta Sky360 Club seats.' Tiered by row: 'Clover Gold (Rows 1-6)', 'Clover Silver (Rows 7 and higher)'. 'All seats ... keep fans within roughly 20 rows of the playing surface.' Individual section pages 11 and 19 both state 'Rows in Section 11/19 are labeled 1-11' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 11'. Ballpark E-Guides: 'The one- and two-digit numbered sections are the low seats behind home plate - club seats that are triple digits in price.' Mets accessibility guide lists accessible seating at 'Sterling Level - Sections 16-18'.

levels.name: Field Level (100 level) - sections 101-143
levels.notes: The lowest general seating tier. Named zones within it, all sourced: Metropolitan Club 111-114 (first base, behind Mets dugout) and 121-124 (third base, behind visiting dugout), 'among the largest in the stadium, featuring up to 32 rows', tiers Platinum/Diamond Rows 1-2, Gold Rows 3-6, Silver Rows 7-12, Bronze Rows 13-22, Box Rows 22+; Hyundai Club 115-117 (first base) and 118-120 (third base), 'just eight rows' per section; Baseline Club Gold/Silver 107, 108, 127, 128 and Baseline Box 104-106 and 129-132; Left Field / Right Field Reserved in the outfield; Big Apple Reserved 140-142 in center field; Citi Pavilion 143 in right-center at Shea Bridge (rows 1-3, group tables of 16-72). Ballpark E-Guides notes '31 is the last row in most sections' at Field Level and that 'Nearly 42% of the seats are located in the lower deck' (Ballparks of Baseball).

levels.name: Empire Suite Level - Sterling Suites 1-10, plus numbered suites (202-243 range referenced)
levels.sections: Sterling Suite 1 - Sterling Suite 10 (listed on the RateYourSeats index under 'All Empire Suites Sections'); also Empire Club and Cadillac Club zone pages exist with no enumerated sections
levels.notes: Suite tier between the field level and the Excelsior Level. RateYourSeats has no individual section pages for these - every Sterling Suite entry links to the /empire-suites zone page. The Mets accessibility guide references this tier as the 'Empire Suite Level' / 'Empire Level' with suites numbered at least 202-243 (e.g. 'Empire Level at Suite 216', 'Party Suites 202-203', 'Suite 227', 'Suite 243', 'across from Suites 204 and 240'). NO general ticketed seating and no home-plate wrap anchor should be configured for this tier.

levels.name: Excelsior Level (300 level, the mezzanine) - sections 301-339
levels.notes: 'Excelsior is the Mezzanine (second) level' (Ballpark E-Guides; the name 'just means higher'). Zones: Coca-Cola Corner 301-305 (right field, up to 16 rows, fully exposed to sun/wind/rain); Excelsior Box 309-312 (first base) and 326-329 (third base); Excelsior Gold = Row 1 of 313-325 (and, loosely, Row 1 of the whole 306-333 run), Excelsior Silver = Rows 2-6 of those sections; The Porch 334-339 (left field, up to 14 rows). 'Sections on the Excelsior Level typically contain no more than 12 rows'; the Gold/Silver core sections have 'just six rows per section'. Piazza 31 Club and the Heineken Diamond Lounge are on this level; the Mets accessibility guide places Heineken Diamond Lounge entrances at Section 315 (first base) and Section 324 (third base). Ballpark E-Guides: 'the outfield sections are covered by the overhang of the upper deck.'

levels.name: Promenade Level, 400 level (lower upper tier) - sections 401-437
levels.notes: 'The Promenade Level makes up the top two seating tiers at Citi Field, consisting of all sections in the 400s and 500s.' 400-level breakdown: Promenade Silver 411-418 (behind home plate; 'provide the most centered sightlines of the diamond and are typically the most expensive seats on the level'), Promenade Baseline 401-410 and 419-428, Promenade Box 429-437. Promenade Gold = Row 1 of every 400- and 500-level section. 'Sections on this level are relatively small, typically containing no more than eight rows' (elsewhere 'between five and seven rows'). Jim Beam Highball Club sits on this level 'behind Sections 411-418'. 'Weather protection is extremely limited on the Promenade Level, and most seats are exposed to sun, wind, and rain.' Ballpark E-Guides places '401 and 501' in 'the right field corner'.

levels.name: Promenade Level, 500 level (highest tier) - sections 501-538
levels.notes: Breakdown: Promenade Infield 510-518 (behind home plate, 'provide the most centered perspective of the field'), Promenade Reserved 506-509 and 519-531, Promenade Outfield 501-505 (right-field side) and 532-538 (left-field side). RateYourSeats 'Upper Promenade Infield' review: 'Most sections feature 17 rows of seating with entry tunnels below the very front row. Coverage is limited, but can be found in the last few rows.' Section 514 page confirms 'Rows in Section 514 are labeled 1-17' with 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 5'. Ballpark E-Guides: 'in the Promenade level sections there are 17 rows to the top of the ballpark'. These are 'the cheapest tickets in the ballpark' and mostly lack club access.

dugouts.home: FIRST BASE SIDE. Ballparks of Baseball Facts & Figures states plainly '-Home Dugout: First Base'. Independently corroborated three times by RateYourSeats: Metropolitan Club - 'Sections 111-114 sit on the first base side directly behind the Mets dugout'; Hyundai Club - 'Sections 115, 116, and 117 run down the first base line ... These sections sit nearest to the Mets dugout'; Delta Sky360 Club - 'Sections AA & A are closest to the Mets dugout' (the AA/A end being the first-base end).
dugouts.visiting: THIRD BASE SIDE. RateYourSeats Metropolitan Club: 'Sections 121-124 are positioned on the third base side directly behind the visiting team dugout.' Hyundai Club: 'Sections 118, 119, and 120 extend down the third base line ... These seats are positioned on the visitor dugout side of the field.' Delta Sky360 Club: 'Sections H & HH are closest to the visitor dugout.'

bullpens: Both bullpens are located beyond the outfield wall in RIGHT-CENTER FIELD, in the area branded 'Bullpen Plaza', beneath and in front of the Shea Bridge. RateYourSeats Citi Pavilion: 'Right-Center Field Location: Situated just beyond the outfield wall near Shea Bridge' and 'Bullpen Views: Positioned directly behind the Mets bullpens' and 'The Citi Pavilion at Shea Bridge is located in right-center field just beyond the outfield wall, positioned near the iconic Shea Bridge walkway and directly behind the bullpens.' RateYourSeats Big Apple Reserved: 'Close to Bullpens: Easy access to Bullpen Plaza with up-close views of pitchers warming up' and 'Guests seated in Big Apple Reserved also enjoy access to Bullpen Plaza, where they can take advantage of picnic-style dining options and close-up views of the Mets bullpens as pitchers warm up.' Ballpark E-Guides: the Citi Pavilion tables sit 'just in front of the Shea Bridge, over the bullpens in right center field', and the Honda Clubhouse group area is 'underneath the right field reserved seats, for a true field-level view of both the field and the bullpen.' The official Mets accessibility guide lists a 'Bullpen Gate - Located off 126th Street (near Roosevelt Ave)' and 'Elevator J: Plaza Level at Bullpen Plaza / Field Level at Section 142'. WHICH bullpen (home vs visiting) is nearer the field is NOT stated by any source consulted; RateYourSeats has a photo captioned 'The visitor bullpen at Citi Field' but does not give its relative position - record as UNKNOWN.

accessibility.summary: The official Citi Field Accessibility Guide states 'All of our ballpark locations are ADA accessible. If an elevator is not available at the entrance, a ramp is available for patrons to take to the nearest level where an elevator can then be accessed.' Citi Field has 11 elevators; 'Guests with disabilities may take elevators to all levels of ballpark.' Accessible seating is sold through all single-game channels (Mets.com, MLB Ballpark App, or the Mets Ticket Office at (718) 507-TIXX), and 'A minimum of one and maximum of three adjacent companion seat(s) may be purchased for each accessible seat purchased. ... The purchase of tickets for accessible seating is restricted to persons who have (or are purchasing tickets for someone who has) a mobility disability or a disability that requires the use of accessible features that are provided in the accessible seating.' ACCESSIBLE SEATING SECTIONS, verbatim from the guide: Sterling Level - Sections 16-18. Field Level - Sections 102, 104, 105, 109-114, 116, 119, 121-125, 129-132, 134-136, 140, 142, and 143. Excelsior Level - Sections 303-305, 308, 312, 317, 321, 326, 328, 330, 335 and 336. Promenade Level - Sections 403, 404, 406-411, 413, 415-417, 419-425, and 428-434. Citi Field also offers 'Movable Armrest Seating' throughout the ballpark - aisle seats immediately upon entering a section where one armrest can be raised; these are flagged under 'More seat details' on Mets.com. Accessibility Services: (718) 565-4360, Accessibility@nymets.com. Fan Assistance Hotline for seat problems: call or text (646) 438-5000. Gates open 90 minutes before each game. Backpacks are not permitted; ADA/medical bag exceptions are made by the Security Supervisor at each entry gate; items no larger than 16x16x8 inches; there is no bag check inside.

row_seat_conventions: ROWS: predominantly NUMBERS, with letters used for the front rows of some field-level sections and lettered rows for ADA access points. Per-level, all verbatim from RateYourSeats section pages unless noted. Sterling Level / Clover Home Plate Club (11-19): 'Rows in Section 11 are labeled 1-11' and 'Rows in Section 19 are labeled 1-11'; RateYourSeats Clover review describes 'Clover Gold (Rows 1-6)' and 'Clover Silver (Rows 7 and higher)' and says all seats are 'within roughly 20 rows of the playing surface'. Field Level (100s): MIXED letters and numbers - Section 126: 'Rows in Section 126 are labeled A-E, 1-34' (i.e. lettered rows A-E in FRONT of numbered row 1); Section 101: 'Rows in Section 101 are labeled 5-15'; Section 132: 'Rows in Section 132 are labeled 24-37'; Section 143 (Citi Pavilion): 'Rows in Section 143 are labeled 1-3'; a Section 133 photo is captioned 'Row D'. Metropolitan Club sections run 'up to 32 rows'. Ballpark E-Guides says '31 is the last row in most sections' at Field Level. The official Mets accessibility guide refers to 'Section 109-Row A' and 'Section 125-Row A', confirming Row A exists as a field-level ADA row. Hyundai Club sections have 'just eight rows'. Excelsior Level (300s): numbers only in everything seen - Section 320: 'Rows in Section 320 are labeled 1-6'; Section 337: 'Rows in Section 337 are labeled 1-12'; sections 'typically contain no more than 12 rows', with the Gold/Silver core at six rows and Coca-Cola Corner up to 16 rows and The Porch up to 14 rows. Promenade 400: Section 415: 'Rows in Section 415 are labeled 1-5'; sections have 'no more than eight rows', typically five to seven. Promenade 500: Section 514: 'Rows in Section 514 are labeled 1-17'; 'Most sections feature 17 rows of seating with entry tunnels below the very front row'; Ballpark E-Guides agrees 'there are 17 rows to the top of the ballpark'. ENTRANCE ROWS vary and are given per section by RateYourSeats ('An entrance to this section is located at Row 15' for 101, 'Row 34' for 126, 'Row 11' for 11 and 19, 'Row 37' for 132, 'Row 3' for 143, 'Row 6' for 320, 'Row 12' for 337, 'Row 5' for 415, 'Row 5' for 514). ACCESSIBLE-ROW LABEL CONVENTION: UNKNOWN. No source consulted states a WC / WCH / VWC / AC suffix or any dedicated wheelchair row label at Citi Field. The Mets guide names accessible SECTIONS but not accessible ROW labels, and describes 'Movable Armrest Seating' as ordinary aisle seats 'located immediately upon entering a section'. SEATS: see seat1_side_verbatim - there is an unresolved conflict between sources.
seat1_side_verbatim: RateYourSeats states, identically on every Citi Field section page checked: "When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the left". Verified verbatim on these section pages: 11 (https://www.rateyourseats.com/citi-field/seating/sections/11), 19, 101, 126, 132, 143, 320, 337, 415 and 514. Note that RateYourseats gives the SAME 'on the left' answer on the first-base side (11), behind home plate (320, 415, 514), on the third-base side (19, 126), in the left-field corner (132), in left field (337), in right field (101) and in right-center field (143) - i.e. RateYourSeats treats seat numbering as running uniformly left-to-right (as the fan faces the field) everywhere in the park. CONFLICTING SOURCE: Ballpark E-Guides states a different rule twice: "Seat 1 in any row is closest to home plate" and, in the obstructed-view section, "Since Seat 1 is always closest to home plate, you should be okay with a higher-numbered seat in a low row." (https://ballparkeguides.com/citi-field-seating/). These two rules AGREE on the first-base side (where home plate is to the fan's left) but DISAGREE on the third-base side and in left field (where home plate is to the fan's right, so a 'closest to home plate' seat 1 would be on the RIGHT, not the left). Both are recorded; neither has been selected. See 'uncertain'.
known_obstructions: NETTING/SCREENING (RateYourSeats fan-feedback note repeated across Citi Field section pages, e.g. sections 11, 19 and 126): "Front of sections 107-128 are behind the netting or fencing - There is some amount of netting or screening in front of sections 107-128. The height and coverage of netting or screening will vary by section. The netting extends from sections 111-124, and there is a protective fence that extends down the right and left field lines until sections 107 and 128." So: full protective netting in front of 111-124 (the home-plate/infield arc), lower protective fencing continuing out to 107 (right-field/first-base line end) and 128 (left-field/third-base line end). PROMENADE GLASS PARTITIONS (Ballpark E-Guides): "in some instances, especially in the Promenade level, glass partitions are placed in a manner that can block as much as a quarter of the field to people sitting in the wrong spot. ... The worst problems by far are in the Promenade Reserved seats past the bases" - the recommended mitigation is "try to get a seat in Row 4 or higher", and the Promenade Gold (Row 1) premium is partly "for the peace of mind of avoiding a glass landing being in front of you". DELTA CLUB BACK ROWS (Ballpark E-Guides): "the last rows of Delta sections have seats in front of aisles, making for an awful obstructed views with people walking in front of you. Avoid Row 20." RIGHT FIELD RESERVED SCOREBOARD BLOCKAGE (Ballpark E-Guides): the Right Field Reserved area "is overlapped by the Coca-Cola Corner - nice on a hot or rainy day but it offers no view of either of the impressive big scoreboards." Similar scoreboard loss is noted for upper rows of covered Excelsior outfield sections: "in the upper rows you may lose some of the big scoreboards." METROPOLITAN CLUB TUNNELS: entry tunnels are at the very TOP of sections 111-114 and 121-124 (up to 32 rows), so low-row occupants have a long walk; conversely RateYourSeats notes the 500-level sections have "entry tunnels below the very front row." The Mets publish a Fan Assistance line for obstructed seats: (646) 438-5000 (Ballpark E-Guides cites the same number and says the Mets "will probably accommodate you").
uncertain: SEAT-1 RULE CONFLICT (highest priority to resolve before generating seat-1 statements). RateYourSeats says 'When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the left' uniformly on EVERY Citi Field section page checked (11, 19, 101, 126, 132, 143, 320, 337, 415, 514) - including sections on the third-base side and in left field. Ballpark E-Guides says 'Seat 1 in any row is closest to home plate' and 'Seat 1 is always closest to home plate'. The two rules coincide on the first-base/right-field side but invert each other on the third-base/left-field side. No official Mets source states a seat-numbering rule. Both recorded verbatim in seat1_side_verbatim; NOT resolved here.

HYUNDAI CLUB SECTION NUMBERS. RateYourSeats (page last verified August 2026) says the Hyundai Club 'is made up of Sections 115-117 and 118-120' - the same 100-series numbering used by the lower-bowl Metropolitan Club sections 111-114 and 121-124, and it describes the Hyundai Club as sitting 'just above the Delta Club and Sterling Suites near home plate'. Ballpark E-Guides describes the Hyundai Club differently, as 'the two lower level areas behind the Delta Club seats at first and third base', without giving section numbers. The official Mets accessibility guide refers to a 'Hyundai Club First Base entrance' at Field Level Section 114 and a 'Hyundai Club Third Base entrance' at Field Level Section 121, which is adjacent to but not inside the 115-120 range. Whether sections 115-120 are a distinct elevated club tier or simply the home-plate arc of the ordinary Field Level bowl is NOT settled. This does not affect direction (all sources put 117 on the first-base side and 118 on the third-base side).

EXCELSIOR-LEVEL HOME PLATE ANCHOR. No source names a single centered 300-level section outright. Section 320 is used as the anchor because its RateYourSeats page carries the 'Home Plate View' insight and the note 'For baseball games, desirable view from behind home plate'; it is also the midpoint of the Excelsior Gold infield range 313-325 and falls between the officially stated first-base (315) and third-base (324) elevator landings. 319 would be an equally defensible anchor. Confidence in the SIDE is very high; confidence in the exact centered section number is medium.

CLOVER HOME PLATE CLUB (11-19) CENTERED SECTION. RateYourSeats states the entire 11-19 run is 'directly behind home plate' but never names the centered section; 15 is the arithmetic midpoint but no source says so. The direction of the 11-19 run is inferred from a single section-19 fan review ('Best seats for fans of the visiting team. Right next to the on deck circle') plus consistency with every surrounding tier; no source states it as plainly as for the other series. Treat 11-19 direction as high-but-not-certain.

DELTA SKY360 CLUB LETTERED SECTIONS. RateYourSeats says 'Sections C & E are centered directly behind the plate' - which implies D sits between them and is the true centre, but RateYourSeats does not say so. The full arc order (AA, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, HH) is inferred from the three positional statements ('AA & A closest to the Mets dugout', 'C & E centered', 'H & HH closest to the visitor dugout') and is not stated as an explicit sequence anywhere.

STERLING SUITES 1-10 / EMPIRE SUITE LEVEL. RateYourSeats lists Sterling Suites 1-10 on the venue section index but every entry links to the /empire-suites zone page rather than to individual section pages, so no per-suite geometry, row data or direction is available. They are EXCLUDED from the 'sections' array. The Empire Suite Level should be given NO home-plate anchor - it is a suite tier, not a ticketed seating bowl, so distances for it should come out blank rather than wrong.

CONCERT FLOOR SECTIONS. RateYourSeats has a 'Field Seats for Concerts' zone at /citi-field/seating/field-seats but does NOT enumerate the individual concert floor section labels anywhere on the venue section index, so none could be recorded. If the generator needs them, they must be scraped from a concert-specific seating chart, not from the venue section index.
CAPACITY SPREAD. 41,922 (Wikipedia body) vs 42,000 (Ballparks of Baseball) vs 41,800 (Wikipedia infobox, 2009-2011 only) vs 45,000+ including standing room (Wikipedia infobox). 41,922 recommended.

COMPASS ORIENTATION rests on a single explicit source (ShadedSeats.com, 'oriented to the north-northeast'). It is consistent with the official Mets gate geography (Right Field Gate on the 1st base side, Left Field Gate on the 3rd base side) and with the 7 Train / Jackie Robinson Rotunda sitting behind home plate, but no official Mets or Wikipedia statement of the compass bearing was found.

BULLPEN OWNERSHIP. Both bullpens are in right-center field beyond the wall at Bullpen Plaza / under the Shea Bridge, and RateYourSeats says the Citi Pavilion sits 'directly behind the Mets bullpens'. Which of the two stacked bullpens is the home one and which the visiting one is NOT stated by any source consulted - record as UNKNOWN.

SECTION 143 vs 140-142 BOUNDARY. Ballpark E-Guides says the numbering 'continues until the Big Apple Reserved seats in center field at 140-142', while RateYourSeats places section 143 (Citi Pavilion) in right-center field near the Shea Bridge. These are compatible (143 continues past centre into right-centre) but no single source states the 140/141/142/143 split explicitly.

SECTION COUNT NOTE. The 'sections' array contains 176 entries (11-19, 101-143, 301-339, 401-437, 501-538, plus the ten lettered Delta/Home Plate Club sections A, AA, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, HH), taken exhaustively from the RateYourSeats venue section index at https://www.rateyourseats.com/citi-field/seating/sections. That index shows no gaps in any numeric run. Zone-only entries with no section pages (Cadillac Club, Empire Club, Field Sections for concerts, Standing Room Only, Sterling Suites 1-10) were excluded.
